facts.statement: The researchers examined large tissue samples from the nasal area of 13 preserved human bodies.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: They used chemical stains and antibody-based techniques to look at specific cell types and how the different layers of the nasal lining connect to each other.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: A special computer program was created to measure the thickness of the tissue and identify the different types of epithelium.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The study found that the three types of nasal lining have different cell mixes and structures, that the olfactory layer varies in thickness compared to the respiratory layer, and that the transitions between them are more complex than what small biopsies show.
facts.subject: cells_or_tissue

facts.statement: The results create a detailed map of the human nasal lining that can serve as a baseline for future research on aging, disease, and smell loss.
facts.subject: humans
